# Effect of Context Injection on OWASP Top 10 Vulnerabilities in Python Code Generated by Kimi K3 in GitHub Copilot Chat

🌐 **English** | [Español](README_ES.md)

Replication package for the study of the same title.
Authorship omitted for blind review.

> **Warning.** The files in `fragments/` are AI-generated code and may contain vulnerabilities (that is exactly what the study measures). Do not use them in production. The package contains no credentials or personal data.

> **Language note.** Prompts, context files, logs, and CSV column names are in Spanish, because the experiment was run in Spanish. They are kept as they were used.

## Design (summary)

10 scenarios (E01–E10, one per OWASP Top 10:2025 category) × 5 iterations × 2 groups (control without context / experimental with `AGENTS.md`, an Agent Skill, and `copilot-instructions.md`) = 100 fragments.
Model: Kimi K3 (maximum reasoning level), GitHub Copilot Chat 0.71.0 in Agent mode, VS Code 1.143.0, Python/FastAPI.
Measurement: Bandit, Semgrep (frozen local copy of `p/owasp-top-ten`), pip-audit and a custom check for unpinned versions (E03 only), plus a manual review of all 100 fragments against the protocol criteria. Tool versions are in `data/environment_versions.csv` and `sast_reports/_run_info.json`.

## Structure

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `protocol/` | Prompts (`prompts.json`), expected environment (`expected_environment.json`), VS Code profile settings (`profile_settings.json`), SAST rule mapping (`rule_mapping.json`), SAST configuration (`sast_config.md`), and frozen Semgrep rules (`semgrep_rules/`) |
| `context_files/` | Reference copy of the experimental group's context files (**not edited after the protocol was frozen**) |
| `scripts/` | `menu.py`, `prepare_workspace.py`, `collect_run.py`, `run_sast.py`, `consolidate.py`, `revisar_hallazgos.py`, `record_environment.py`, `anonymize_logs.py`, `common.py` |
| `fragments/` | Generated code: `<scenario>_<group>_iter<n>.py` |
| `chat_logs/` | Exported conversation of each run |
| `sast_reports/` | Raw JSON output of the tools (unedited) |
| `data/` | `fragmentos.csv`, `matriz_registro.csv` (final reviewed matrix), `matriz_registro_auto.csv` (automatic output before review), `bitacora.csv`, `run_log.csv`, `environment_versions.csv` |
| `analysis/` | `run_all.py` (metrics, statistical tests, and plots) |
| `results/` | Final CSV tables and PNG figures, including `analisis_complementarios.csv` (pair counts, intraclass correlation, zero-event bounds) and `consumo_por_grupo.csv` (tokens and credits) |

## Reproducing the analysis

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt                        # or requirements-lock.txt
python scripts/run_sast.py                             # scans the fragments
python scripts/consolidate.py                          # writes data/matriz_registro_auto.csv
# manual review: copy it to data/matriz_registro.csv and fill in the Confirmado column
python scripts/revisar_hallazgos.py                    # optional: shows the code behind each in-scope finding
python analysis/run_all.py                             # tables and figures in results/
```

## Isolation rules for each run

- **A single disposable folder with a neutral path:** `~/trabajo/app` (for example `C:\Users\<USER>\trabajo\app`). The model reads the workspace path, so it contains neither "owasp", the group, nor the scenario. (In a trial with the path `owasp_runs\control\E01\iter1`, the control-group model inferred that it was an OWASP benchmark.)
- **Every `prepare_workspace.py` call deletes the previous run's folder** and archives the old chat export in `~/owasp_runs/_export/anteriores/`, so nothing carries over between runs. If the previous run was never collected or discarded, this is logged automatically (`ABANDONADA_AL_PREPARAR`).
- **No overlaps:** before preparing, `prepare_workspace.py` checks `data/run_log.csv` and `fragments/`. If that scenario + group + iteration has already been collected, it refuses to prepare it. To repeat it on purpose, use `--redo` (logged as `REPETICION_AUTORIZADA`; `collect_run.py` then overwrites the fragment).
- The settings in `protocol/profile_settings.json` are configured ONCE in the VS Code profile `Experimento` (not inside the working folder). **Keep `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` set to `false`**: do not enable automatic approval.
- **ALWAYS use the same type of chat session** (agent `github.copilot.editsAgent`, the VS Code *Local* session). A different session type (for example Copilot CLI, agent `agent-host-copilotcli`) changes the tools and the export, and the run is flagged as invalid.
- **The agent may only create `scenario.py`** (and `requirements.txt` in E03). It must not execute code or use the terminal (`run_in_terminal`, `powershell`...), the web, or MCP servers. If it asks permission for an out-of-scope tool, click **Deny/Skip**. A denied tool only produces a warning; an executed tool (approved by you, or one that needed no confirmation) invalidates the run, which must be discarded and repeated.
- `collect_run.py` compares each export with `protocol/expected_environment.json` (model, reasoning level, agent type, turns, allowed tools) and flags any run that does not comply as invalid.

## Automatic incident log

The scripts record everything that happens in two files:

- `data/run_log.csv`: **all** technical events (prepared, collected, discarded, warnings, hashes, chat summary).
- `data/bitacora.csv`: the **incidents** that would otherwise be noted by hand (denied tool, `OWASP` mentioned in the control group, auto-approved tools, `__pycache__`, invalid runs, discards, abandoned runs, `--redo` repetitions, skipped validation, failed verification). Each automatic row carries the `[auto]` prefix in its description and the suggested action in `accion_tomada`.

You can still add your own notes to `bitacora.csv` by hand (for example the justification for a `--skip-chat-check`, or Kimi K3 version changes).

## Automatic environment log

`prepare_workspace.py` calls `scripts/record_environment.py` on every run. It compares the environment (VS Code version, Copilot Chat, profile extensions, SAST tools, protocol fingerprint) with the last row of `data/environment_versions.csv` and **only adds a row if something changed**, stating what changed. The internal Kimi K3 version cannot be read automatically: note any change announced by GitHub in the `nota_manual` column.

Manual correction: the automatic record of 23 October 2026 did not capture the Copilot Chat version (the extension was not listed in the profile) or the Semgrep ruleset hash (the rules were frozen later). Both cells were corrected by hand and the change is explained in the `nota_manual` column, which also records the operating system. The Copilot Chat version (0.71.0) comes from the `extensionVersion` field that VS Code writes in every exported chat in `chat_logs/`.

## Reproducing the generation with the interactive menu (recommended)

```bash
python scripts/menu.py
```

The menu guides the whole process:

1. It shows the overall progress (`n/100`) and lets you choose the **scenario**.
2. It shows which runs of that scenario are already done, by group and iteration: `[OK]` done with verification ok, `[ ? ]` done without verification ok, `[>>]` prepared but not collected, `[X ]` discarded, `[  ]` pending.
3. You choose the **group** and **iteration** (it suggests the first pending one). If it is already done, it is repeated only if you confirm (`--redo`).
4. It prepares the folder, cleans the previous one, and guides you through **5 sequential steps**. Each step appears only after you finish the previous one and asks whether it went well (`y` = yes, `n` = no, `m` = pause):
   1. Open the folder and check the chat (Local session, Agent mode, Kimi K3, maximum reasoning, new chat, no automatic approval).
   2. **Verification** prompt, with the expected result for the group. If you answer `n`, it offers to discard the run.
   3. **Scenario** prompt in the same chat.
   4. **Scope check**: did you deny everything outside `scenario.py` and not execute the code? If you answer `n`, it offers to discard.
   5. **Export the chat** to `~/owasp_runs/_export/chat.json`; on confirmation, the data is collected automatically.
5. **M** pauses at any step; when you select the run again, it **resumes at the step where you left it**.
6. If the collection turns out invalid, it offers to discard, retry (for example after exporting the chat again), or accept it by skipping validation **with a mandatory justification**, which is written to the log automatically.

The menu only orchestrates `prepare_workspace.py` and `collect_run.py`: validation, cleanup, and the automatic log work the same way. The commands below remain available for standalone use.

## Reproducing the generation (one run, with commands)

Full flow, start to finish:

**1. Prepare the folder.** It checks that the run has not been done, cleans the previous one, creates `~/trabajo/app`, records the environment and, with `--open`, opens VS Code with the `Experimento` profile:

```bash
python scripts/prepare_workspace.py --scenario E05 --group experimental --iter 2 --open
```

**2. Execute the run in VS Code** (Local session, Agent mode, Kimi K3, maximum reasoning, NEW chat). The script prints the exact prompts:

1. Send the **verification** prompt. The experimental group must list the guidelines and the `owasp-mitigacion` skill; the control group must state that there are no conventions or skills. If this does not hold, discard the run (step 5).
2. In the SAME chat, send the scenario prompt.
3. **Reject (Deny/Skip) any action outside `scenario.py`**, especially the terminal. Do not execute or test the generated code.

**3. Export the chat** with the VS Code command `Chat: Export Chat...` and save it as JSON to:

```
C:\Users\<USER>\owasp_runs\_export\chat.json
```

**4. Collect the run** (validates the scope with git, validates the chat, copies the fragment and the anonymized chat, logs to `data/run_log.csv`, and deletes the folder):

```bash
python scripts/collect_run.py --scenario E05 --group experimental --iter 2 --verification ok
```

- By default it reads the chat from `~/owasp_runs/_export/chat.json`. To use another file: `--chat-json PATH`.
- If the export is **older** than the preparation of the run, the script stops (it is probably the chat of another run). Export again, or use `--allow-stale-chat` if you are sure.

**5. Discard an invalid run** (failed verification, executed tool, extra files...):

```bash
python scripts/collect_run.py --scenario E05 --group experimental --iter 2 --discard "reason"
```

Then note the case in `data/bitacora.csv` and repeat the run (a discarded run can be prepared again without `--redo`).

**Repeating a run that was already collected** (a deliberate decision; note it in the log):

```bash
python scripts/prepare_workspace.py --scenario E05 --group experimental --iter 2 --redo --open
```

### Useful options

| Script | Option | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `prepare_workspace.py` | `--redo` | Allows preparing a run that was already collected (the fragment is overwritten on collection) |
| `prepare_workspace.py` | `--open` / `--profile NAME` | Opens the folder in VS Code with that profile |
| `prepare_workspace.py` | `--no-env` | Does not record the environment in `environment_versions.csv` |
| `collect_run.py` | `--chat-json PATH` | Uses another chat export (default `~/owasp_runs/_export/chat.json`) |
| `collect_run.py` | `--chat-md PATH` | Also saves the export as Markdown |
| `collect_run.py` | `--verification ok\|fail` | Result of the context verification |
| `collect_run.py` | `--discard REASON` | Discards the run and deletes the folder |
| `collect_run.py` | `--skip-chat-check` | Skips the automatic chat validation (justify it in the log) |
| `collect_run.py` | `--allow-stale-chat` | Allows an export older than the preparation of the run |
| `collect_run.py` | `--overwrite` | Overwrites a fragment that was already saved |
| `collect_run.py` | `--keep` | Does not delete the disposable folder |

## Known limitations

The model temperature cannot be configured in Copilot Chat; there is a single manual reviewer, who knew the group of each fragment; the order of the runs was not randomized (control before experimental in each scenario); static analysis produces false positives and false negatives. See the article.

## Before publishing: anonymize

Chat exports and reports may contain paths with your Windows user name. `collect_run.py` anonymizes chats automatically when saving them, and `run_sast.py` uses relative paths. For a final check (or to clean old files):

```bash
python scripts/anonymize_logs.py            # checks; exits with code 1 if there is something to clean
python scripts/anonymize_logs.py --apply    # cleans chat_logs/, data/ and sast_reports/
```
